Rule:
ID: TRANSITION
Title: Post-termination transition assistance and data return
Kind: missing
Summary: When it ends, we get our data back and help moving.
Severity: medium
Category: transition
Position — preferred:
On expiry or termination, Vendor provides transition assistance for up to 6 months at then-current rates, returns Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days, and certifies deletion thereafter.

Position — fallback:
90 days of transition assistance; data export within 30 days.
Position — walk-away:
No data return, or immediate deletion of Customer Data on termination.
Detection guidance:
Look for transition, exit, data return/export, deletion timing. Absence in a services/hosting agreement is a deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a transition-assistance and data-return paragraph in the termination section.
Model language:
Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days, return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.


Claimed finding status: missing

Finding rationale:
This hosted-services MSA contains no post-termination transition-assistance or data-return obligation. Section 10.1 merely assumes "any agreed transition period" without creating a right to one, and Section 10.2 covers only Deliverables and refunds. Section 16.5's return-or-destroy duty expressly carves Customer Data out to "Sections 11 and 15" — there is no Section 11 in the Agreement, and Section 15 addresses only processing restrictions and privacy compliance, not return, export format, or deletion timing. Neither the preferred nor the fallback position (90 days' assistance plus export within 30 days) is met, so we insert a new Section 10.3 at the preferred position: up to six months' transition assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, machine-readable return of Customer Data within thirty days, and certified deletion thereafter (with the customary backup/legal-retention carve-out already used in Section 16.5). Ninety days' assistance is available as a fallback.

Original paragraphs:
p0041: 10.1 On expiry or termination, Customer's right to access terminated subscription Services ends after any agreed transition period. Rights in accepted Deliverables, paid-up licences, Customer Data, and materials Customer owned or licensed independently continue according to their terms.
p0042: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
p0063: 16.5 On request or termination, the recipient shall return or destroy Confidential Information, subject to routine backups and legal retention. Duties for trade secrets continue while protected as trade secrets; duties for other Confidential Information continue for five years after disclosure. Customer Data remains governed by Sections 11 and 15.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Vendor: This Master Services Agreement (this “Agreement”) is entered into as of 1 January 2026 (the “Effective Date”) by and between Juniper Ridge Health, Inc., a Delaware corporation with offices at 100 Hudson Street, New York, New York 10013 (“Customer”), and Cobalt Cloud Services LLC, a New York corporation with offices at 250 Park Avenue, New York, New York 10177 (“Vendor”). Customer and Vendor are each a “Party” and together the “Parties.” In consideration of the mutual promises set out below, the Parties agree as follows.
Customer Data: 1.3 “Customer Data” means all data, records, files, content, personal information, and other materials submitted to, stored in, transmitted through, or otherwise made available to the Services by or for Customer or its Authorized Users, together with output specifically derived from that material. Customer Data excludes anonymized operational telemetry that cannot reasonably be linked to Customer, an Authorized User, or an individual.
Deliverable: 1.4 “Deliverable” means each report, configuration, integration, specification, design, workflow, training material, and other work product that an Order Form identifies as being created specifically for Customer. Deliverables exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how retained in the unaided memory of Vendor personnel.
Fees: 1.5 “Fees” means the recurring subscription fees, professional services fees, usage fees, and other amounts payable by Customer under an Order Form for the Services during the applicable period. Fees do not include taxes, reimbursable expenses, service credits, interest, damages, or a one-time implementation charge unless an Order Form expressly states otherwise.
Services: 1.7 “Services” means the hosted software, implementation, configuration, support, maintenance, consulting, and related services described in an Order Form. Services include all corrections, updates, and generally released improvements Vendor provides without an additional licence fee to similarly situated customers purchasing the same service tier.
Confidential Information: 16.1 “Confidential Information” means non-public information disclosed by or for a Party that is marked confidential or that a reasonable recipient would understand to be confidential given its nature and the circumstances. Customer Data, security information, product plans, pricing, personnel data, and the terms of this Agreement are Confidential Information whether or not marked.

Rendered redline:
p0042: 10.2 Vendor shall deliver all completed and in-process Deliverables for which Customer has paid or agrees to pay the applicable proportionate Fees. Vendor shall refund prepaid recurring Fees covering the period after termination, together with Fees paid for Services Customer cannot reasonably use because of Vendor's uncured breach.
10.3 Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Order Form for any reason, Vendor shall (a) at Customer's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Vendor's then-current rates; (b) within thirty (30) days of Customer's request, return or make available for download all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (c) thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems, subject to routine backups and legal retention requirements, and certify such deletion to Customer in writing.

Comment:
[Playbook] We added an orderly exit provision: up to six months of transition assistance at your then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a machine-readable format within thirty days, and certified deletion afterwards. The Agreement currently has no data-return or exit-assistance obligation (Section 16.5 defers Customer Data to Sections 11 and 15, neither of which addresses return or deletion), and we cannot migrate off a hosted service without it. If six months is too long, we can accept ninety days of assistance.

**To:** Deal team
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Legal review of the Master Services Agreement against our playbook

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have completed our playbook review of the Master Services Agreement. The commercial architecture of the deal is broadly acceptable — the liability cap, licence grant, warranty package, assignment rights, audit rights, renewal mechanics and Vendor insurance all sit at our preferred position and require no redline. The problem is concentrated in two places: (i) a set of one-way restrictive covenants and commitments imposed on us, and (ii) material omissions.

The single most serious issue is that the Agreement contains **no indemnity at all**. There is no Section 20, yet four separate clauses (§ 9.3, § 19.4, § 21.3, § 30.5) cross-refer to indemnities as if one existed — including § 9.3's reference to "Section 20.5" for IP infringement remedies. We have no defence or hold-harmless protection for third-party IP claims, and the drafting is internally broken.

Separately, § 12.4 (which appears twice), § 7.2 and § 2.1 load us with a three-year USD 2,000,000 per-year take-or-pay commitment "without reduction or termination rights", a worldwide 24-month post-term non-compete, a 24-month no-hire covering *all* Vendor employees, and an open-ended duty to disclose and match any better third-party offer. Each of these sits in walk-away territory, and each directly contradicts § 12.3, in which the Vendor expressly acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, no-hire, minimum-volume or most-favoured-customer commitment. That internal contradiction is our strongest negotiating lever: we are asking the Vendor to conform the operative text to a representation it has already made.

We also have no termination-for-convenience right across a three-year term, no post-termination transition assistance or data-return mechanic, Vendor ownership of Deliverables we pay for, and a Singapore governing law clause that conflicts with the New York venue clause immediately beneath it (§ 28.1 vs § 28.2).

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following sit in walk-away territory under our playbook. We should not sign without resolution of each.

1. **No Vendor indemnity (missing § 20).** No IP, legal-compliance, data-breach or misconduct indemnity exists, while § 9.3, § 19.4, § 21.3 and § 30.5 all assume one does. We must have a Section 20 with IP remedies numbered 20.5 to make § 9.3 operable.
2. **Three-year, USD 2,000,000 per-year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights" (§ 2.1).** Multi-year lock-in with no reduction or exit mechanism.

4. **Worldwide 24-month post-term non-compete on us (§ 12.4).** Undefined scope, sweeping in acquisitions and internal development.
5. **Exclusive-dealing covenant (second § 12.4).** Term plus 24 months, all territories, no category limit, no performance-based exit.
6. **One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees (§ 12.4).** Overrides general-advertising and unsolicited-application carve-outs.
7. **Customer-side MFN / duty to disclose and match (§ 7.2).** Open-ended obligation to extend better third-party terms to Vendor.
8. **Exclusive Singapore governing law and jurisdiction (§ 28.1).** Outside the accepted list, and in direct conflict with § 28.2.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline with the § 12.3 conflict up front.** Lead the cover note with § 12.3 and ask the Vendor to conform § 2.1, § 7.2 and both instances of § 12.4 to the acknowledgement it has already given. This is a consistency argument, not a concession request, and is the cheapest path to five of the eight walk-away items.
2. **Insert Section 20 (Indemnification) as drafted.** Flag that § 9.3's cross-reference to "Section 20.5" is currently a dead reference and that our numbering restores it; this is presented as a drafting repair as well as a substantive ask.
3. **Add § 9.4 (termination for convenience)** — 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no reciprocal Vendor right — with an express override of § 2.1.
4. **Reverse § 14.2 Deliverable ownership** to us with Vendor assignment, expressly preserving Vendor background IP and the § 13.2 embedded-IP licence. Fallback if resisted: a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables.
5. **Insert § 10.3 (transition and data return)** — up to six months' assistance at Vendor's then-current rates, machine-readable return within 30 days, certified deletion with the § 16.5 backup/legal-retention carve-out. Fallback: 90 days' assistance. Note separately that § 16.5 cross-refers to a non-existent Section 11 and needs correcting.
6. **Amend § 28.1** to New York law and New York County courts, aligning it with § 28.2 and leaving § 28.3 escalation intact.
7. **Confirm no further movement is sought** on the liability cap, assignment, licence grant, warranty, audit, renewal, insurance and no-LD provisions. These sit at our preferred position and we should protect them in any horse-trading.
8. **Escalate the two commercial items** — the § 2.1 volume commitment and the § 12.4 restrictive covenants — to the business owner before the next negotiation session, so we know our authority on the fallbacks (12-month reducible commitment with true-up; narrowed term-only non-compete; mutual 12-month non-solicit).

*This memo is based solely on the verified findings listed above. Section references are as they appear in the Agreement, including the duplicate numbering at § 12.4 and the missing Sections 11 and 20.*"}
